definition: No method — the highest means without a means. In Kashmir Śaivism, anupāya is the state where no spiritual progress, no contemplation, no recitation, no practice is needed. It is named by performance, not by label. Abhinavagupta devoted Tantrāloka ch.2 to anupāya.

sources.claim: Anupāya = no method; the highest means without a means. The devotee does not need meditation, concentration, or recitation.

In this highest state of supreme God consciousness (anuttara) there is no need of spiritual progress, no contemplation, no art of expression, no investigation, no meditation, no concentration, no recitation, exertion or practice.

translations.note: Anupāya is not a technique added to the six denied; it is the recognition that no technique is needed. Staying (yathāvasthita) is the method that is no method. (Anuttarāṣṭikā v.1)
